question.text: The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] \approx 2.2778,$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x^2}{12}, & 0 < x < 2, \\[5pt] % this part integrates to 2/9 \dfrac{7}{9}, & 2 \leq x < 3,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_0^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^2 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx + \int_2^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^2 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{x^2}{12} \, \textrm dx + \int_2^3 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{7}{9} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^2 \dfrac{x^4}{12} \, \textrm dx + \int_2^3 \dfrac{7x^2}{9} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{x^5}{60} \right|_0^2 + \left. \dfrac{7x^3}{27} \right|_2^3 \\[5pt] &\approx 5.4593 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &\approx 5.4593 - (2.2778)^2 \\[3pt] &\approx 0.271 \end{align*}\] rounded to three decimal places.

question.text: Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{4}{x^5}, \quad &x \geq 1,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

First, we compute $\textrm E[X]{:}$

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X] & = \int_{1}^\infty x \cdot \dfrac{4}{x^5}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^\infty \dfrac{4}{x^4} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \left( - \dfrac{4}{3x^3}\right) \right|_{1}^\infty \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{3} \end{align*}\]

Then, we compute $\textrm E[X^2]{:}$

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_{1}^\infty x^2 \dfrac{4}{x^5} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^\infty \dfrac{4}{x^3}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \left(- \dfrac{2}{x^2} \right) \right|_{1}^\infty \\[5pt] &= 2 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= 2 - \left(\dfrac{4}{3} \right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{9}. \end{align*}\]

question.text: The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] \approx 3.314\,81,$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{9}, & 0 < x < 3, \\[5pt] % this part integrates to 2/9 \dfrac{1}{9}(2x-5), & 3 \leq x < 5,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_0^5 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^3 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx + \int_3^5 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^3 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{9} \, \textrm dx + \int_3^5 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{9}(2x-5) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^3 \dfrac{x^2}{9} \, \textrm dx + \int_3^5 \dfrac{1}{9}(2x^3-5x^2) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{x^3}{27} \right|_0^3 + \left. \dfrac{1}{9}\left(\dfrac{x^4}{2}-\dfrac{5x^3}{3}\right) \right|_3^5 \\[5pt] &\approx 13.074\,07 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &\approx 13.074\,07 - (3.314\,81)^2 \\[3pt] &\approx 2.09 \end{align*}\] rounded to $2$ decimal places.

question.text: The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\textrm E[X] \approx 1.136\,90,$ compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} x, & 0 \leq x < 1, \\[5pt] % this part integrates to 1/2 \dfrac{3x^2}{14}, & 1 \leq x \lt 2,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

We compute $\textrm E[X^2],$ as follows:

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_0^2 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx + \int_1^2 x^2 \cdot f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^2 \cdot x \, \textrm dx + \int_1^2 x^2 \cdot \dfrac{3x^2}{14} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 x^3 \, \textrm dx + \int_1^2 \dfrac{3x^4}{14} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right|_0^1 + \left. \dfrac{3x^5}{70} \right|_1^2 \\[5pt] &= 1.578\,57 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the variance is given by

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &\approx 1.578\,57 - (1.136\,90)^2 \\[3pt] &\approx 0.29 \end{align*}\] rounded to $2$ decimal places.

question.text: Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\textrm{Var}[X].$ \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{30(x-1)}{x^7}, \quad & x \geq 1,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

First, we compute $\textrm E[X]{:}$

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} x \cdot \dfrac{30(x-1)}{x^7} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac{30x-30}{x^6}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac{30}{x^5}- \dfrac{30}{x^6}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= - \dfrac{30}{4x^4} + \dfrac{30}{5x^5}\Bigg|_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= - \dfrac{15}{2x^4} + \dfrac{6}{x^5}\Bigg|_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2} \end{align*}

Then, we compute $\textrm E[X^2]{:}$

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} x^2 \cdot \dfrac{30(x-1)}{x^7} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac{30x -30}{x^5}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{\infty} \dfrac{30}{x^4}- \dfrac{30}{x^5}\, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= - \dfrac{30}{3x^3} + \dfrac{30}{4x^4}\Bigg|_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= - \dfrac{10}{x^3} + \dfrac{15}{2x^4}\Bigg|_{1}^{\infty}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{2} \end{align*}

Therefore, the variance is given by

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E [X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{2} -\left( \dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}. \end{align*}
